newsitem.title: ITALY: Edison profits up, sees further gains.
newsitem.headline: Edison profits up, sees further gains.

text.p: Italy's largest private energy producing group Edison on Monday reported a 57 percent jump in first half 1996 profits and promised further increases in profits for the rest of the year.

The company which produces energy for industrial users and supplies state-owned ENEL utility with electricity, reported first half pre-tax 1996 profits of 395 billion lire ($260 million), up from 252 billion, on turnover up 39 percent at 920 billion lire.
The profits were aided by the sale to state-controlled oil concession for 98 billion lire, which led to a gain of 68 billion.
But the group, which is 61.33 percent owned by Italian agro-industry and chemicals group Montedison SpA, forecast higher profits for the second half of 1996 and also for the full year 1996 over 1995.

Edison continued to look to the future, with investments up at 360 billion lire for the first half from 145 billion and even above the 1995 figure of 345 billion. This caused debt to edge up to 797 billion lire from 740 billion at end-1995.

At the parent company level, net operating profits at Edison SpA slipped to 52 billion lire from 80 billion on turnover down 15 percent due to reduced income from hydroelectricity after poor rainfall in the first half, and also when compared to the first half of 1995, when the company had a capital gain from its sale of its stake in MonteShell. ($1=1,521 lire)
